title: Kamarajar's Wealth: An Empty Pocket and Unblemished Integrity
summary: When former Chief Minister K. Kamaraj passed away in October 1975, the state discovered that nine years of executive power had left him with only a few khadi dhotis and a hundred rupees.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 198: நேருவும் “நான் அப்போது இருந்தேன்; நீங்களோ?” என்ற பதிலும்
full_text:
On October 2, 1975, in a modest rented house on Tirumalai Pillai Road in Chennai, a monumental chapter in Indian history came to an end. K. Kamaraj passed away quietly in his sleep.

For nine unbroken years, he had governed Tamil Nadu as Chief Minister; subsequently, as President of the Indian National Congress, he was venerated across the world as the 'Kingmaker' who guided the succession of Prime Ministers Lal Bahadur Shastri and Indira Gandhi.

When government officials and executors formally inventoried his worldly estate, they stood in stunned reverence.

The entire worldly possessions of this statesman consisted of:
Six worn pairs of hand-spun khadi dhotis and shirts, one spare pair of spectacles, a modest umbrella, two worn pens, and one hundred and thirty rupees in cash!
He owned no private bungalow, no real estate, no corporate shares, and no family trust. Even when his elderly mother lived in Virudhunagar, Kamaraj had refused to allow local municipality officials to install a special water tap at state expense, sending her a small money order from his personal salary each month.

In an era where political office is too often equated with personal enrichment, Kamaraj’s empty pockets and unblemished integrity stand as an eternal monument to public service.

moral: Selfless integrity is the supreme crown of leadership; true wealth is an unblemished conscience dedicated to the people.
